Well folks, once again we see the fundamental disconnect between out-of-touch cultural elites and the hard-working people who actually build and sustain our communities. We are looking at a petition drive launched last month called Water Not Coal, started by Corb Lund, aimed at tying the hands of the Government of Alberta with top-down legislation to "prohibit through legislation all coal exploration." 

Now, let’s look at what is really at stake here. Southern Alberta’s watershed is vital, of course—nobody values family, land, and the God-given resources of our country more than traditional conservatives. But we have to ask ourselves: who is driving these panic-driven crusades against economic independence and industrial self-reliance? It’s the same crowd of cultural agitators and celebrity-led movements pushing an agenda that weakens our traditional industries and leaves working families vulnerable to bureaucratic control. 

Instead of trusting local organizers and petitions backed by cultural figures to dictate economic stagnation, we need to respect the lawful authority of our government and the time-tested pillars of industrial enterprise that keep our nation strong and self-sufficient. Personal responsibility and respect for order mean letting our institutions work without yielding to the alarmism of progressive lifestyle campaigns.

source_text:
Folks, let’s call this out for what it really is. Last month, a petition drive called Water Not Coal was started by Corb Lund, aimed at tying the hands of the Government of Alberta with top-down legislation to "prohibit through legislation all coal exploration." 

This is just another alarmist crusade pushed by cultural agitators and celebrity-led movements that threatens our economic independence, undermines industrial self-reliance, and leaves working families vulnerable to bureaucratic control. Southern Alberta’s watershed is vital, but instead of bowing to these progressive lifestyle campaigns and petitions backed by cultural figures that aim to dictate economic stagnation, we must respect the lawful authority of our government and the traditional pillars of industrial enterprise. It is time to stand up for personal responsibility, respect for order, and the strength of our nation.

Folks, let’s call this out for what it really is. Last month, a petition drive called Water Not Coal was started by Corb Lund, aimed at tying the hands of the Government of Alberta with top-down legislation to "prohibit through legislation all coal exploration." 

This is just another alarmist crusade pushed by cultural agitators and celebrity-led movements that threatens our economic independence, undermines industrial self-reliance, and leaves working families vulnerable to bureaucratic control. Southern Alberta’s watershed is vital, but instead of bowing to these progressive lifestyle campaigns and petitions backed by cultural figures that aim to dictate economic stagnation, we must respect the lawful authority of our government and the traditional pillars of industrial enterprise. It is time to stand up for personal responsibility, respect for order, and the strength of our nation.
